form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Welch (for himself, Mr. Merkley, Mr. Booker, Mr. Van Hollen, and Mr. Sanders) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation

form.official-title: To eliminate toxic substances in beverage containers, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Banning Toxics from Plastic Bottles Act of 2026.

paragraph.text: The term Administrator means the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency.

subparagraph.text: The term beverage means any drinkable liquid intended for human oral consumption, including—

clause.text: any other beverage determined to be appropriate by the Administrator.

subparagraph.text: The term beverage does not include—

clause.text: a drug regulated under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 301 et seq.);

subparagraph.text: The term beverage container means a prepackaged container that—

clause.text: is designed to hold a beverage;
is made of any material, including glass, plastic, and metal; and
has a volume of not more than 3 liters.

subparagraph.text: The term beverage container does not include—

clause.text: aseptic packaging, such as a drink box.

subparagraph.text: The term brand means any mark, word, name, symbol, design, device, or graphic element that—

clause.text: distinguishes the product from other products.
any combination of 2 or more marks, words, names, symbols, designs, devices, or graphic elements described in subparagraph (A); and

subparagraph.text: The term plastic means a synthetic or semisynthetic material that is—

clause.text: synthesized by the polymerization of organic substances; and
capable of being shaped into various rigid and flexible forms.

subparagraph.text: The term plastic includes any coating or adhesive described in subparagraph (A).

paragraph.text: The term product line means a group of related products marketed under a single brand name that—

subparagraph.text: is sold, offered for sale, or distributed by a distributor in the United States, including through an internet transaction; and
is used by the distributor for the purpose of distinguishing those products from other, similar products for better usability for consumers.
The term retailer means an entity located in the United States that—

clause.text: engages in the sale of beverage containers to a consumer; or
provides beverage containers to an individual or entity in commerce, including provision free of charge, such as at a workplace or event.

subparagraph.text: The term retailer includes an entity located in the United States that engages in the sale of, or provides, beverage containers as described in subparagraph (A) through a vending machine or similar means.

paragraph.text: The term single-use, with respect to a beverage container, means that the beverage container is routinely disposed of, recycled, or otherwise discarded after 1 use.

subparagraph.text: The term toxic substance means any substance, mixture, or compound that—

subclause.text: personal injury or disease to humans through ingestion, inhalation, or absorption through any body surface; or
adverse impacts on the environment; and

clause.text: satisfies 1 or more of the conditions described in subparagraph (B).

subparagraph.text: The conditions referred to in subparagraph (A)(ii) are the following:

clause.text: The substance, mixture, or compound is subject to reporting requirements under—

subclause.text: the Emergency Planning and Community Right-To-Know Act of 1986 (42 U.S.C. 11001 et seq.);
the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (42 U.S.C. 9601 et seq.); or
section 112(r) of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7412(r)).

clause.text: The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, the National Toxicology Program, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the Administrator of Health and Human Services, the National Institute for Environmental Health Sciences, or the Environmental Protection Agency has established that the substance, mixture, or compound poses an acute or chronic health hazard, including developmental, reproductive, or endocrine effects.

The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health or the Environmental Protection Agency has recognized that the substance, mixture, or compound may increase the risk of developing a latent disease.
The substance, mixture, or compound is—

subclause.text: a bisphenol compound (but not including an alkyl-substituted bisphenol compound generated through a xylenol-aldehyde process);
a halogenated or nanoscale flame-retardant chemical;
listed as a persistent organic pollutant by the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants;
given an overall carcinogenicity evaluation of Group 1, Group 2A, or Group 2B by the International Agency for Research on Cancer; or

listed as a toxic, poisonous, explosive, corrosive, flammable, ecotoxic, or infectious waste by the Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and Their Disposal, done at Basel, Switzerland, March 22, 1989.

clause.text: The substance, mixture, or compound is a chemical or chemical class that, as determined by the Administrator, has been identified by a Federal agency, State agency, or international intergovernmental agency as being 1 or more of the following:

subclause.text: A carcinogen, mutagen, reproductive toxicant, immunotoxicant, neurotoxicant, or endocrine disruptor.
A chemical or chemical class that may—

item.text: harm the normal development of a fetus or child or cause other developmental toxicity in humans or wildlife;
harm organs or cause other systemic toxicity; or

subclause.text: A chemical or chemical class that has toxicity equivalent to the toxicity reflected in a criterion described in any of subclauses (I) through (III).

section.header: Elimination of toxic substances and other substances that prevent recyclability in beverage containers

subsection.text: Effective beginning on the date that is 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, no retailer may sell, offer for sale, or distribute any single-use beverage container that—

paragraph.text: is composed wholly or partially of polyethylene terephthalate glycol;
is opaque or pigmented a color other than transparent blue or transparent green;
A retailer that violates a prohibition under subsection (a) shall be subject to a fine for each violation.

For purposes of this section, each product line of beverage containers shall be considered to be a separate violation of this section if any beverage container included in the product line is a beverage container described in subsection (a).
The amount of a fine under this subsection shall be not more than $50,000 per violation.
Fines collected under this subsection shall be deposited into the Local Clean Up of Plastics Fund established by section 4(a).

section.header: Grants to local governments for solid waste and water system infrastructure improvements

subsection.text: There is established in the Treasury of the United States a fund, to be known as the Local Clean Up of Plastics Fund.

Amounts in the Fund shall be available to the Administrator, without further appropriation or fiscal year limitation, to make competitively awarded grants to units of local government for projects to make improvements to solid waste infrastructure, water system infrastructure, recycling facilities, and composting facilities, for the purpose of increasing the rate of diversion of waste from landfills or complying with environmental regulations relating to such infrastructure or facilities, including—

paragraph.text: educational programming relating to such infrastructure or facilities.

subsection.text: In making grants under subsection (b), the Administrator shall give priority to projects that would serve—

paragraph.text: a rural area (as defined in section 203(b) of the Rural Electrification Act of 1936 (7 U.S.C. 924(b))); or
an underserved community, as determined by the Administrator.
